correctness.rationale: Integer parity follows from evenness of central binomial coefficients. Coefficientwise mod-2 Frobenius plus repeated squaring gives exact 2^k separated-block congruences. The doubling-index terms are Cauchy, limit 3 mod 8. A valuation argument gives maximal order 2^(k-2) in the index-two unit subgroup, and index construction realizes powers and 7-times-powers at infinitely many n. Explicit boundary cases k=1,2 are reductions from k=3. Standalone checks corroborate finite cases, not replace proof.

originality.rationale: Originality at best available evidence: the result determines all residue images modulo powers of two with infinite representations; inspected parity, general sum congruences, Gauss congruences and prime-modulus digit laws do not entail the claimed surjectivity. No directly covering research-record result was found. Unindexed stronger general constant-term results remain a historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: An earlier general theorem about constant terms of Laurent powers modulo prime powers might imply the same unit-group image without using the phrase central trinomial.
Historical priority is not certified by a negative semantic search; specialist review of additional older literature remains appropriate.

value.rationale: Classifying all dyadic residue images and infinite occurrence for the natural central trinomial sequence solves a full invariant, rather than providing merely first terms or known parity. Explicit separated-block lifts and the 2-adic unit-generator mechanism explain the classification, creating a useful structural starting point for distribution questions.
